about: Worked example for docs/15: Akbar's accession and his reign, filling gap-list items 2 and 3.

events.name: Akbar Becomes Mughal Emperor
aliases: Akbar the Great takes the throne
events.description: The thirteen-year-old Akbar is proclaimed Mughal emperor at Kalanaur in the Punjab after his father Humayun dies from a fall. With his guardian Bairam Khan as regent, his army defeats Hemu at Panipat months later, securing the throne and opening a reign that would expand and transform the Mughal Empire.
events.note: Enthroned 14 February 1556 (some sources give his formal coronation slightly later). Humayun died in January 1556.
events.significance: Akbar's reign turned a fragile, newly restored dynasty into the dominant power of the subcontinent. His conquests, his mansabdari system of ranked officers and his policy of religious accommodation, including ending the jizya tax on non-Muslims, gave the Mughal state a structure his successors built on for a century.

spans.name: Reign of Akbar
spans.description: Akbar's half-century as Mughal emperor, when conquest, a reformed administration and religious tolerance made the empire the dominant power of the subcontinent.
spans.note: Ends with his death in October 1605.

links.why: Humayun died months after retaking Delhi, and his son Akbar succeeded him.
